title: Meta says AI is making it easier to build new apps — and more are coming
slides: Meta says AI speeds app creation—but at what cost?
Their internal tools now generate functional code from prompts.
Yet these apps often fail outside Meta's engineered ecosystem.
You can prototype faster, but debugging becomes unpredictable.
Test each AI-built module separately before trusting the whole.
thread_text:
1. Faster code, at what price?

Meta's internal tools generate working apps from prompts alone.

2. The ecosystem trap.

These apps break outside Meta's own platforms.

3. Speed hides risk.

Prototyping shortcuts unpredictably extend debugging.

4. Test the atoms first.

Each AI module needs separate validation before integration.

5. Check your own stack.

Take a prompt from ChatGPT and simulate a build. Does the gain justify the fix?

script: Meta says AI speeds app creation.

instagram.caption:
Meta's own internal tools now build working apps from nothing but a prompt.  

Those same apps crash the second they leave Meta's curated environment. 🛠️  

Prototyping gets faster—debugging becomes a maze. Every fix pulls a new thread.  

You can build faster, but you'll spend twice the time patching code your tool wrote blind.  

Before you trust the whole, test each AI-generated module alone. ⚙️ Does your stack save time or create more problems?
